answer: One saffron harvest from a karst terrace buys a seat only when the lagoon below vouches for the water. At first light, a newcomer picks a single marked bed and dries its stigmas in the sun, while two lagoon wardens weigh the dried threads against the bed's yield table and check the karst spring that fed it still runs clear. Threads short by more than a gram, or a spring running muddy, voids the claim and forfeits a 600 POA deposit. Each bed costs a $190 lease plus $55 per warden, so a hundred fakes would mean a hundred beds, $30,000 in fees and 60,000 POA locked in deposits.
